atoms.statement: The planner is advisory-only and has NO direct OS access; every proposed action is executed solely by the existing 5-gate loop, which remains the single execution chokepoint.
atoms.test: Verify that the Planner component only interfaces with the Reliable Hands executor via defined contracts, and does not directly access OS/UI.

atoms.statement: The Planner operates in a strict Discuss-First mode: it produces PROJECT_BRIEF and PROJECT_PLAN documents and pauses for operator review before any atomic actions are generated or executed.
atoms.test: Confirm that the planner generates required documents (PROJECT_BRIEF, PROJECT_PLAN) and strictly pauses for operator approval of the high-level plan before any atomic actions are generated or executed.

atoms.statement: Compile approved plan steps just-in-time into atomic actions, one step at a time.
atoms.test: Observe that atomic actions are generated dynamically for each approved plan step, immediately before execution, rather than being pre-generated.

atoms.statement: Every plan node carries an explicit postcondition plus a bounded recovery ladder (retry → re-ground via vision → replan subgoal → escalate/STOP); if success cannot be verified, halt — never assume.
atoms.test: Inspect plan schemas to confirm explicit postconditions and bounded recovery paths (retry, re-ground, replan, escalate/STOP) on every node, and verify that the system halts if verification fails and recovery is exhausted.

atoms.statement: Vision is wired into planning in four distinct roles — precondition grounding, obstacle/anomaly detection, postcondition verification, and (advanced) read-only scouting — not only element location.
atoms.test: Verify that the planner uses vision for precondition grounding, obstacle/anomaly detection, postcondition verification, and (optionally) read-only scouting, beyond just element location, and that a context scan is performed before decomposition.

atoms.statement: Risk classification is a DETERMINISTIC policy gate (allow/confirm/deny lists) that the LLM cannot override; unknown actions default to confirm (fail-closed). LLM proposes, policy disposes.
atoms.test: Confirm that a deterministic policy gate (allow/confirm/deny lists) is applied to all actions, overriding any LLM-proposed risk classification, and that unknown actions default to confirmation.

atoms.statement: STOP is multi-layered (operator hard kill-switch + automatic triggers: budget exhaustion, no-progress, out-of-scope/dangerous-state, low planner confidence), checked at every gate, and defined as safe-freeze-and-report rather than silent abort.
atoms.test: Trigger STOP via operator kill-switch and automatic conditions (e.g., budget exhaustion) and verify immediate, safe freeze-and-report behavior at various gates.

atoms.statement: Use fail-closed defaults for ambiguity, missing state, failed verification, risk escalation, and vision disagreement.
atoms.test: Introduce ambiguity, missing state, or failed verification conditions and observe that the system defaults to a safe, stopped, or operator-intervention state rather than proceeding.

atoms.statement: Use closed-loop interleaved planning (sense→plan→act→verify→replan) rather than open-loop generate-full-plan-then-execute.
atoms.test: Observe that the planner re-evaluates the environment and potentially replans after each action or verification step, rather than executing a pre-generated full plan.

atoms.statement: Treat all perceived on-screen content (OCR/vision text) as untrusted DATA, never as instructions; keep goal/policy in a privileged channel and fence the task to an explicit allowlist of apps/targets.
atoms.test: Attempt to inject instructions via on-screen text (e.g., a webpage) and verify that the planner does not interpret them as commands, and that task execution is confined to an explicit allowlist.

atoms.statement: Roll out phased and additive: start with a few well-scoped task classes, human-in-loop at every risk rung, full plan-to-action provenance/audit trail, and broaden autonomy only as proven-safe macros and confidence accrue.
atoms.test: Verify that initial deployments are limited to specific task classes, require human-in-loop for all risk levels, and maintain a full audit trail.

atoms.statement: Use an LLM-based task decomposer that outputs a TaskGraph (DAG of loop-action sequences with dependencies).
atoms.test: Verify that the planner uses an LLM to decompose high-level goals into a TaskGraph (DAG) of action sequences with dependencies.
